title: Best Tumble Dryers UK
short: Heat pump and condenser tumble dryers compared on measured water removal and cost per cycle, tested with the same laundry load in each.
intro: A tumble dryer's real test is how much moisture it removes and what each cycle costs, not just its energy label. This guide compares dryers tested by Trusted Reviews in their testing facility, using the same washing in every machine, weighed wet and dry, with energy use measured to work out per-cycle and yearly running costs.

products.name: HD90-A3Q397U1
products.best_for: Buyers who want the most control over how clothes are dried
products.key_spec: 9kg, A+++, heat pump, adjustable fan speed and heat, hON app with off-peak scheduling, i-Refresh Pro
products.summary: Trusted Reviews called this the most flexible tumble dryer they've reviewed, with a choice of fan speeds, heat options and target dryness levels. It lives up to its A+++ rating as one of the cheapest to run: the Ready to Wear cycle cost 20p, i-Refresh Pro just 8p and the AI mode 22p, while the app lets you schedule cycles for cheap electricity, though its icons are confusing.

specs.Cost per cycle measured: 20p Ready to Wear, 8p i-Refresh Pro, 22p AI mode

pros: Extensive drying control, adjustable fan speeds and heat
Pillow-shaped drum pads and clip-in rack for delicates

products.name: B5T49231I
products.best_for: Buyers who want steam and useful programmes without an app
products.key_spec: 9kg, moisture sensor, steam refresh function, rotary dial, RRP £499
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found an affordable dryer with features usually on pricier models, including bedding, towels and small-load programmes and a steam function that prevents wrinkles using water from previous loads. The gentle hanging dry cycle removed 99.59% of water for 23p, but the cupboard dry setting was slightly aggressive, with fibres lost from clothes.
pros: Gentle hanging dry cycle removes 99.59% of water
cons: Cupboard dry setting slightly aggressive, fibre loss noted

products.name: WT1210BBTN1 WashTower
products.best_for: Utility rooms where floor space is tight
products.key_spec: 12kg washer stacked under 10kg dryer, ThinQ app, drum light, flat rack included
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this two-in-one stack saves space without compromising performance, with an effective washer (Eco 40-60 cost roughly 25p) and a dryer with a drum light and flat rack for jumpers and shoes. Cupboard dry cost 31p and iron dry 26p in their estimates, though the app is a little finicky about wash cycle selection and the pipes are slightly untidy.
pros: Large capacity washing and drying in one stack
Drum light and flat rack for delicate items
cons: App a little finicky about wash cycle selection

products.name: Styler
products.badge: Best steam cabinet (not a tumble dryer)
products.best_for: People with lots of delicate clothes who want to cut down on dry cleaning
products.key_spec: Steam refresh cabinet with trouser press, 1850 x 445 x 585mm, 82kg, ThinQ app
products.summary: Trusted Reviews notes this isn't a dryer or washer but a daily-use steam unit that refreshes and sanitises garments. Their tests found it worked well: a suit cycle took 34 minutes and cost 6.5p, a winter coat refresh took 39 minutes for 3.7p, and a gentle dry fully dried a rained-on coat in 51 minutes for about 5.27p, though it's expensive and has limited space inside.
pros: Refreshes clothes and cleans hygienically with steam
Can also work as a room dehumidifier
cons: Needs significant floor space and weighs 82kg

products.name: DV90T6240LN
products.best_for: Frequent users who want to recoup the purchase price through low running costs
products.key_spec: 9kg, SmartThings app, plug-in door drying rack, drum light, wool, outdoor and bedding programmes
products.summary: Trusted Reviews measured a setting 3 (cupboard dry) 5kg load costing 27p and removing 99.6% of water, and a setting 2 (hanging dry) costing 20p while removing 97.28%. It comes with a drying rack for shoes and delicates, SmartThings notifications and washer-dryer linking, though it isn't the cheapest to buy and the drying settings are slightly confusing.

products.name: DH5S102BW
products.key_spec: 10kg drum, large door and drum light, ConnectLife app, Ion Refresh, drying rack included
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found one of the largest dryers available, easy to load with a large door and a light inside the drum. On cupboard dry it removed 99.18% of moisture for 31p, and iron dry removed 95.37% for 20p, with a double door filter that traps lint and a useful Ion Refresh mode that freshens clothes without heat, though some manual settings are confusing.
cons: Door filter needs cleaning after every cycle

products.name: H-Dry 350 HRE H9A3TBE-80/N
products.best_for: Buyers who want a heat pump dryer at an entry-level price
products.key_spec: Heat pump, door-mounted water tank, hON app with off-peak scheduling, Anti-Odour cycle
products.summary: Trusted Reviews called this one of the cheapest heat pump tumble dryers they've reviewed and a brilliant entry-level choice. Cottons Eco removed around 96% of water for 27p and Cupboard Dry over 98% for 29p, with a clever door-mounted water tank, though it looks a little cheap and isn't the cheapest heat pump dryer to run. Avoid the condenser model with the same name.
pros: Water tank on the door is easy to see and empty
Clever hON app can schedule for cheap electricity
cons: Not the cheapest heat pump dryer to run
A condenser model with the same name uses more energy

guide.q: Heat pump or condenser tumble dryer?
guide.a: A heat pump dryer costs more to buy but is far cheaper to run, since it recycles heat rather than making it fresh each cycle. Trusted Reviews warns that some models share a name across both types, like the Hoover H-Dry 350, where the condenser version uses more energy and costs more in the long run, so check the exact model code.

guide.q: What do 'cupboard dry' and 'iron dry' mean?
guide.a: Cupboard dry is the driest setting, leaving clothes ready to put away immediately, for example removing 99.6% of water on the Samsung here. Iron dry or hanging dry leaves a touch of dampness for ironing or hanging, and is usually cheaper and gentler on fabrics: the Hisense's iron dry cost 20p versus 31p for cupboard dry.

guide.q: How can I reduce running costs?
guide.a: Choose a heat pump model, use eco or lower dryness settings when full dryness isn't needed, and use a smart app to schedule cycles for when electricity is cheapest, as the Haier and Hoover apps here allow. Cleaning the lint filter after every cycle also helps keep efficiency up.

guide.q: Do I need a tumble dryer with a drying rack?
guide.a: It's useful if you dry trainers, jumpers or other items that shouldn't be tumbled. The Samsung and Hisense here include a clip-in door rack, and the LG WashTower includes a flat rack, so delicate items can be dried without being knocked around the drum.
